parts.given_text: After the brief impulse, the body moves at constant speed I/m. No subsequent force acts.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two identical blocks start from rest at the same height. One falls vertically; the other slides down a straight frictionless slope inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal, where 0 < θ < 90°. Both reach the ground with the same speed. Which reaches the ground first?

answer.text: The vertically falling block arrives first. Its acceleration is g; the sliding block has acceleration g sin θ and travels a longer distance. tslide = tfall/sin θ > tfall.

ibd-c0351bd864435118-q3:whole.hint: Try listing the known motion quantities first. Which constant-acceleration equation leaves only the quantity you need?
notes: For constant acceleration, use v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² or v² = u² + 2as. Choose the equation that avoids an unknown you do not need.

fep-060f4d71e7cb832b-q2:whole.hint: Compare the spread of repeated readings separately from their closeness to the accepted value.
notes: Precision describes agreement between repeated readings; accuracy describes agreement with the accepted value. A tightly clustered set can still be systematically wrong.

fep-060f4d71e7cb832b-q3:whole.hint: Choose one vertical positive direction and identify the initial vertical velocity.
notes: Ignoring air resistance, vertical acceleration is constant and downwards. Use s = ut + ½at² or v² = u² + 2as with a consistent sign convention.
At the highest point of an upward throw, velocity is momentarily zero but acceleration remains downwards. Falling time in this model does not depend on mass.
